title: Solar Orbiter Experiment Interface Document Part A
organisation: European Space Agency (ESTEC), Solar Orbiter Team
status_notes: Issue 1 Revision 0 of 9 October 2007, prepared by the Solar Orbiter Team (book captain Danielle Renton) and approved by Philippe Kletzkine (PDF pp. 1-2); the change log and change record are empty and the status field is blank. Section 1.2 says the EID is first released with the instrument Announcement of Opportunity and placed under configuration control once signed. This is a pre-selection (study phase) issue: many subsections, especially operations and data interfaces, are 'TBD' or 'TBW', and the reference payload and resources were later superseded.
summary:
The first issue of Part A of the Solar Orbiter Experiment Interface Document (EID-A), released by ESA/ESTEC with the instrument Announcement of Opportunity in 2007. EID-A states the technical and programmatic requirements that every Principal Investigator's instrument must meet. Part B, written by each PI, answers it and becomes the binding agreement, and both parts become applicable to the prime contractor.

The document begins with programme background (Cosmic Vision, the joint mission with NASA's Inner Heliospheric Sentinels), the project document tree and the ESA contacts. Section 3 describes the spacecraft as then conceived: perihelion down to 0.22 AU, a heat shield, X-band and Ka-band communications through a steerable HGA, New Norcia as baseline ground station, payload allocations of 180 kg, 180 W and 100 kbps, and a table of candidate instruments (SWA, RPW, MAG, EPD, DPD, VIM, EUS, EUI, COR, STIX, HI/WFC) with their mass, power and data rate. It also covers thermal control and the data handling architecture, in which a data management system is the instruments' gateway to ground over dual cold-redundant SpaceWire links.

Section 4 holds the instrument interface requirements: labelling, lifetime, coordinates, alignment, mechanical, thermal, electrical, SpaceWire data handling (including reception of SpaceWire time codes), 18 software design rules (boot software in PROM, memory areas, event reports on resets and errors, single-TC enabling of uploaded software), EMC, handling and environment. Sections 5 to 8 cover operations (mostly TBW), verification and testing, product assurance and management. Section 9 lists normative ECSS/PSS and informative references. For telemetry and telecommand engineers its value is historical: it shows the Solar Orbiter instrument data interface before PUS and MIB details were defined.

contents.title: Materials and Process Selection and Control

key_points.text: The EID has two parts: EID-A gives the Solar Orbiter technical and programmatic requirements all PIs must comply with; EID-B is the PI's response and the sole binding agreement between the ESA project office and each PI. Both go under formal configuration control once signed and become applicable to the prime contractor.
In 2007 the mission was planned for a 2015 launch, with an ESA-NASA joint mission combining Solar Orbiter and NASA's Inner Heliospheric Sentinels; the Call for Letters of Intent drew 23 responses.
The near-Sun phase brings the spacecraft as close as 0.22 AU.

Communications assumption: X-band and Ka-band transponders with parallel telemetry downlink via a 2-degree-of-freedom steerable HGA, X-band LGA for LEOP, New Norcia as baseline ground station and Cebreros as backup.
Remote sensing instruments operate in three 10-day windows per orbit (around perihelion and at highest northern and southern latitudes), while in situ instruments operate continuously.
Payload allocations: 180 kg mass, 180 W power and 100 kbps data rate.

Candidate instrument data rates in the 2007 table include SWA 14 000 bps, RPW 5 000 bps, MAG 800 bps, EPD 3 100 bps, STIX 200 bps and EUI 20 000 bps, for a total of 106 100 bps that exceeds the allocation.

The data management system provides instrument command and control, command timeline management, packetised science data acquisition, mass memory storage and transmission to ground, and health monitoring of instruments that are off.
Instruments interface with the spacecraft data handling system through a dual cold-redundant SpaceWire interface (ECSS-E-50-12) for TM transmission and TC reception.
Instruments shall be able to receive SpaceWire time codes (ECSS-E-50-12), and each instrument shall support 2 independent SpaceWire lines routed separately to the spacecraft DHS.

On-board software shall comply with ECSS-E-40, keep a minimum boot software in PROM from which all functions are accessible, use separate memory areas for code, constants and variables, and allow uploaded software to be checked before it is enabled by a single telecommand.

Any communication between ground and an on-board software function shall use purpose-designed TC and TM source packets, and the software shall generate event reports before forced resets and on overload, arithmetic overflow, illegal instruction, data bus error, EDAC memory corruption and checksum error.

The MOC supplies PIs in near real time with raw instrument data plus spacecraft HK and auxiliary data, performs out-of-limit checks on a set of payload parameters and notifies anomalies to the SOC and PIs; inputs to the satellite database are still 'TBW'.

notes: Text-based PDF with 200 pages (the text extraction shows a 201st, empty page); printed page numbers ('page n of 200') match PDF page indexes. The title page text is garbled by a decorative font ('OLAR RBITER XPERIMENT NTERFACE OCUMENT ART'), and the title was read as 'Solar Orbiter Experiment Interface Document Part A'. Section 2.1 prints ESA staff telephone numbers and e-mail addresses, which are deliberately omitted here. NR2 and NR6 both cite ECSS-E-50-12. Section 4.10.1 points to a 'Section 3.6.3' for EMC performance requirements. Many operations and data-interface subsections (5.2.2, 5.3.2, 5.3.3 'Inputs to Satellite Database', 4.8.2.4 'Digital Telemetry') are TBW or TBD. It predates instrument selection; the operational SWA and STIX databases in the library (swa-idb-ascii, swa-idb-v6-5-0, stix-idb-v2-26-38-raw) and the SWA DPU ICD (so-swa-dpu-cd-ic-003-dpu-communications-interface-control-document-issue8-2) reflect the later, implemented interfaces. Hosted on a NASA explorers.larc.nasa.gov page (file name prefix '12_3').
